en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Gabbhinīvagga 62.
The Training Rule on Nursing Mothers:
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, nuns were giving the full admission to a woman who was breastfeeding.
She went out for alms,
and people said this:
“Alms for the noble lady; the noble lady has a companion.
People complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying, “How can these bhikkhunīs give the full admission to one who is breastfeeding?”
The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, criticizing, and grumbling.
Those bhikkhunīs who were few in desires... [and so on]... complained, criticized, and grumbled:
"How can these bhikkhunīs give the full admission to one who is breastfeeding?"... [and so on]...
“Is it true, monks, that nuns are giving the full admission to a woman who is breastfeeding?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... [as before]...
"How indeed, monks, can bhikkhunīs give the full admission to a woman who is nursing?
This, monks, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of those with faith...

And furthermore, monks, let the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule: 'Whatever bhikkhunī should give the full admission to a woman who is nursing, that bhikkhunī is to be dealt with according to the rule.'"
“Whatever nun, however, should give the full admission to a woman who is nursing [an infant], that is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).
“Whatever nun” means whichever nun of such a kind... [and so forth].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"One who is giving birth" means:
"Either a mother or a nurse.
"Should ordain" means: should confer full admission.
If she seeks out a group, a preceptor, an alms-bowl, or a robe, thinking, “I will ordain her,” or if she demarcates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
For the motion (ñatti), there is an offense of wrong-doing;
for each of the two formal proclamations (kammavācā), there is an offense of wrong-doing.
At the conclusion of the formal act (*kammavācā*), the preceptor incurs an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*);
the community and the senior teacher (*ācarinī*) incur an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
If she gives the full admission to one who is breastfeeding, perceiving her as such, she incurs an offense of expiation.
If she gives the full admission to a woman who is breastfeeding while being uncertain [of her status], there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).

If she gives the full admission to a woman who is breastfeeding while perceiving her as not breastfeeding, there is no offense. If she gives the full admission to a woman who is not breastfeeding while perceiving her as breastfeeding, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If she is breastfeeding and one is doubtful, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If she is breastfeeding and one perceives her as such, there is no offense.
There is no offense—
If she ordains one who is nursing while perceiving her as not nursing,
or if she ordains one who is not nursing while perceiving her as not nursing, or in the case of one who is insane; [there is no offense].
"For one who is a first offender.
The second training rule is concluded.
